titulo: Si (if) followed by past tenses in the indicative
subtitulo: Si ha llovido, habrá charcos. Si iba al centro, gastaba mucho.
regla: Si + past indicative presents the condition as real or very likely: Si llovió anoche, la calle estará mojada. Si iba al salón, gastaba mucho (whenever). Si never takes the future or the conditional.

bloques.texto: **Si** + **indicative** (present or past) treats the condition as **real or likely**.

lista.texto: A real possibility about the past: **si tuvo un accidente, no va a venir**.
Often _whenever_, a past habit: **si iba al centro, gastaba mucho**.

bloques.texto: **Si** never takes the **future** or the **conditional**: ~~si irás~~, ~~si iría~~.
Compare: **si** + imperfect subjunctive = unreal: **si tuviera dinero, viajaría**.
Tip: indicative **si** = maybe it really happened.

lista.es: ==Si ha llovido== mucho, las calles van a tener charcos.
lista.en: If it has rained a lot, the streets will be full of puddles.

lista.es: ==Si iba== a la estética, gastaba mucho dinero.
lista.en: Whenever I went to the salon, I spent a lot of money.

lista.es: ==Si tuvo== un accidente, no va a ir a trabajar esta semana.
lista.en: If he had an accident, he won't go to work this week.
If you got there late, I'm sure they scolded you.
If you didn't study, don't complain.

filas.t: Si irás al centro, compra pan.
Si vas al centro, compra pan.
Si llovió, el pasto está mojado.
Si hubiera llovido, el pasto estaría mojado.

bloques.texto: Say it out loud, then open the answer.

lista.p: In Spanish: _If he left at six, he'll be here soon._
lista.r: Si salió a las seis, va a llegar pronto.

lista.p: In Spanish: _Whenever I was bored, I read._
